skills.name: Accounting for transactions with trade bills

note.text:
A trade bill (effet de commerce), such as a bill of exchange or a promissory note, is a written promise or order to pay a sum on a fixed date (maturity).
Seller (drawer) who draws a bill on a customer:
• Bill accepted: debit 412 Customers, bills receivable; credit 411 Customers.
• Bill paid at maturity: debit 521 Bank; credit 412.
Buyer who accepts a bill: debit 401 Suppliers; credit 402 Suppliers, bills payable. Paying it at maturity: debit 402; credit 521 Bank.
Advantages: a clear date and legal proof of the debt; the seller can get cash earlier by discounting the bill at a bank.

sections.heading: Paying later, in writing
sections.text:
When a customer cannot pay at once, the seller may ask for a trade bill (effet de commerce): a document in which the customer promises, or is ordered, to pay a sum on a fixed date, the maturity date.
Bills of exchange and promissory notes are common trade bills. They give legal proof of the debt and a clear payment date.

sections.heading: The seller's entries
sections.text:
• When the customer accepts the bill, the debt changes form: debit {'412 Customers, bills receivable'}, credit {'411 Customers'}.
• At maturity, when the bill is paid: debit {'521 Bank'}, credit {'412'}.
If the seller needs cash before maturity, it can discount the bill at a bank and receive the amount less interest.

sections.heading: The buyer's entries
sections.text:
• Accepting a bill drawn by a supplier: debit {'401 Suppliers'}, credit {'402 Suppliers, bills payable'}.
• Paying it at maturity: debit {'402'}, credit {'521 Bank'}.
Each side moves the debt from the ordinary account ({'411'} or {'401'}) to the bills account ({'412'} or {'402'}).

key_words.meaning: a written promise or order to pay on a fixed date
account {'412'}: bills the business will collect
account {'402'}: bills the business must pay

mistake.wrong: The seller records a new sale when the bill is accepted
mistake.right: Accepting a bill only changes the form of the existing debt: Dr {'412'} / Cr {'411'}
mistake.why: The sale was recorded earlier; the bill is just a new way of owing.

worked_example.problem: A customer owes {t} FCFA and accepts a bill of exchange for this amount, due in {60} days. Give the seller's entries now and at maturity.
steps: Bill accepted: debit {'412 Customers, bills receivable'} {t}; credit {'411 Customers'} {t}.
At maturity, when paid: debit {'521 Bank'} {t}; credit {'412'} {t}.

cards.idea: A trade bill is a written promise or order to pay on a fixed date.
example: A bill of exchange due in {90} days

cards.idea: The seller moves the debt from {'411'} to {'412'} Bills receivable.
The buyer moves the debt from {'401'} to {'402'} Bills payable.

check.prompt: At the start of the month, {'412'} Bills receivable has a balance of {o} FCFA. Bills of {a} FCFA are accepted by customers and bills of {p} FCFA are paid. What is the closing balance (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Accepted bills increase the balance; paid bills decrease it.

solution: Bills paid decrease it: {o + a} − {p} = {answer} FCFA.

pick.r: A written promise or order to pay a sum on a fixed date
w: A receipt for cash already paid
e: It is about a future payment.
pick.y: Bills of exchange and promissory notes are trade bills.

pick.q: What is the maturity date of a bill?
pick.r: the date on which it must be paid
w: the date the goods were made
pick.y: The bill is payable on its due date.

pick.q: Which is an advantage of a trade bill for the seller?
pick.r: It is legal proof of the debt and can be discounted at a bank for cash
w: The customer never has to pay
It is a sale of the business
e: The customer must pay at maturity.
pick.y: It gives security and access to cash.

pick.q: SELLER: a customer accepts a bill of 300 000 FCFA for what he owes.
pick.r: Dr 412 Customers, bills receivable / Cr 411 Customers
e: No money has been received yet.
pick.y: The debt becomes a bill receivable.

pick.q: SELLER: the bill of 300 000 FCFA is paid at maturity into the bank.
pick.r: Dr 521 Bank / Cr 412 Customers, bills receivable
e: The debt was already moved to 412.

pick.q: BUYER: the business accepts a bill of 250 000 FCFA drawn by its supplier.
pick.r: Dr 401 Suppliers / Cr 402 Suppliers, bills payable
pick.y: The debt becomes a bill payable.

misconceptions.explain: Accepted bills increase the balance; paid bills decrease it.

solution: Bills paid decrease it: {o + a} − {p} = {answer} FCFA.

questions.prompt: A bill dated 1 March (non-leap year) is payable {n} days later. Counting 1 January as day 1, what is the day number of its due date?

misconceptions.explain: Count the days in January and February too: {1} March is day {60}.

solution: 1 March is day {60} of a non-leap year ({31} + {28} + {1}).
